title: ANAC Precedent Inconsistency — Investigation of LATAM KPI Manipulation (2023) vs. Rejection of Passenger Complaint (2024‑2025) Violating Constitutional Principle of Isonomy
incident_timestamp_display: 3 December 2025 — ANAC dismissal of NUP 50001.115849/2025‑10, contrasted with 2023 investigation of LATAM
allegation_summary: ANAC actively investigated LATAM for KPI manipulation practices in 2023, acknowledging the airline’s pattern of regulatory fraud. Yet, when the same passenger filed a complaint in 2025 documenting identical KPI manipulation (8 case numbers for one incident) by the same airline, ANAC dismissed the complaint (NUP 50001.115849/2025‑10), claiming lack of jurisdiction. This contradictory treatment violates the constitutional principle of isonomy (CF/88 Art. 5, caput), which guarantees equal treatment under the law. ANAC cannot exercise jurisdiction to investigate corporate misconduct in one instance and then refuse to protect a consumer in an identical factual scenario. The inconsistency also breaches the administrative principles of morality, reasonableness, and security of legitimate expectations (Lei 9.784/99, Art. 2), undermining public trust in the regulatory system.
